title: Inject an OS file picker into a service
summary: A service asks for the operating system's file picker by injection. `tac.nativeCapabilities: ["filePicker"]` in `client/manifest.json` grants it, separately from `tac.browserApis`. Without the grant, every call answers `denied` before a panel opens. The grant does not replace the user's choice or the signing entitlements: a sandboxed macOS app also needs the user-selected read-only file entitlement, and Tachyon does not add it for you. `open` lets the user choose one file; the only type filters are `text/plain` and `application/json`, and an empty list allows any file. The answer holds the file name and an opaque handle, never a path. `readText(handle)` reads at most 65,536 bytes of UTF-8 text, and `release(handle)` ends access. A handle belongs to the service that asked for it. It ends after 300 seconds, or sooner when that service goes away. Every answer is a typed status (`selected`, `cancelled`, `read`, `released`, `denied`, `unsupported`, `unavailable`, `invalid`, `disposed` or `tooLarge`); nothing throws. The picker opens a panel (NSOpenPanel) in a macOS app, for JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust and Swift services, the Windows file dialog (IFileOpenDialog) in a Windows app, for JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust and C# services, and the GTK file dialog, or the desktop portal's chooser where one runs, in a Linux app, for JavaScript, TypeScript and Rust services, the document picker (UIDocumentPickerViewController) in an iOS app, for JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust and Swift services, and the system document picker (ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT) in an Android app, for JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust and Kotlin services (ADR 0089). A Swift, C# or Kotlin service that runs as WebAssembly in an app (C# and Kotlin on macOS and iOS, Swift and Kotlin on Windows, Swift and C# on Android, all three on Linux) reaches the same picker through the page. The iOS simulator and Android emulator runs are still owed. A browser tab opens no panel and answers `unsupported`. JavaScript and TypeScript inject `filePicker` with `@Needs` and get Promises. Rust declares a `FilePicker` field in a `Default` service. Swift, C# and Kotlin ask for an uninitialized `FilePicker` field with `NeedsAll`. Every service uses the same file on every target. In a browser tab, the field of a Swift, C# or Kotlin service is still filled: `available()` is false and every call answers `unsupported`. Options that break the contract, such as more than one file or another type, still answer `invalid`. The page never passes a `filePicker` property. Dart, Go, Ruby, Java, F# and Python services have no FilePicker provider yet, so this feature has no tab for them; a `NeedsAll` FilePicker field there stays a page property, and the build stops with `TY1407` when the page does not pass it. A Lua service has no FilePicker: a `---@type FilePicker` field in a Lua service stops the build with `TY2015`. C++ has no FilePicker either: a C++ `Needs` field may name Tachyon's browser APIs, but `FilePicker` is not one of them, so such a field stops the build with `TY1372`. Let a JavaScript, TypeScript or Rust service use the picker and send the text to the other services with an event.
